newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Weather steady in Brazil's key soybean areas-coops.
newsitem.headline: Weather steady in Brazil's key soybean areas-coops.

text.p: Brazil's soybean crop was developing favorably with rain expected at the weekend in some areas and temperatures moderately warm, cooperatives said.
Growers said there was a generalized plague of caterpillars in most soybean growing areas but added it was well under control.
Torrential rains this week in Parana State affected mainly low-lying regions and left the soybean crop unscathed, according to Otmar Hubner at the Parana agricultural secretariat.
"We had three or four days of heavy rains but it hasn't affected soybeans," Hubner said. "The crop is only beginning to mature. It it rains a lot next month, then it will be a problem."
Several growers in Parana reported that forecast rains failed to materialise on Friday, but skies were partly cloudy. Temperatures ranged between 20 and 30 degrees Celsius.

Farmers in the key growing region of Rio Grande do Sul were hopeful that rainfall would normalise following a period of dryness earlier in the year. Temperatures there ranged between 15 and 25 degrees C.
"Rain is forecast for the weekend," said Guiomar Backes, agronomist at the Coopermil cooperative in Santa Rosa. "The only inconvenient is the caterpillar plague but it's under control."
Agronomists reiterated that corn had suffered much more from the recent dry spell than soybeans.

Edaleceo Cobadte, agronomist at the Cotrisan cooperative in Sananduva, said the corn planted in October would suffer a 20 percent crop loss but corn planted in August and September was virtually unaffected.
Cobadte added that he expected weather conditions to normalise now and he saw no threat of a fall in the soybean harvest. --Joelle Diderich, Rio de Janeiro newsroom +55 21 407 4151
